item.title: Alan Patrick set for his smallest role at Inter since returning
item.description: Alan Patrick set for his smallest role at Inter since returning A doubt for next Tuesday’s (3rd) clash with Coritiba, midfielder Alan Patrick finds himself in an unusual situation in 2026. This season is on course to be his quietest in terms of appearances, minutes played and goal contributions, counting only the years in which he played a full season for Internacional, according to data compiled by ge. The No. 10 caused concern among fans when he was substituted in the 88th minute of the defeat to Fluminense, a match in which he scored. After feeling pain in his right thigh, the player will undergo a further medical assessment to determine his fitness for the next round of fixtures. So far, Alan Patrick has featured in 40 of Inter’s 51 matches in 2026, totaling 2,899 minutes. His nine goals and eight assists fall short of his figures for 2023, 2024 and 2025, according to ge. It is worth noting that the analysis considers only full seasons, as the player arrived at Beira-Rio midway through 2022. Despite the decline in his numbers, the captain’s influence remains undeniable. He is tied as the squad’s second-highest scorer this year alongside Borré—who is no longer at the club—and Vitinho, all with nine goals, behind only Bernabei’s 10. Alan Patrick is also the team’s leading provider, topping the assists chart outright. The new tactical approach and the captain’s role Regarded as one of the dressing-room leaders and the squad’s standout technical talent, Alan Patrick struggled at the start of the year. Under Paulo Pezzolano, Internacional adopted a more reactive tactical approach in the Brasileirão. With a system focused on physicality and defensive work, the classic No. 10’s style fell out of favor, costing him his place in the starting lineup. The midfielder endured five consecutive matches on the bench without even being called upon by the Uruguayan coach. Recently, however, the situation has taken a turn. With Eduardo Baptista’s arrival as head coach, Alan Patrick has regained a central role and started four of the last five matches, repaying that trust with two goals and an assist. One curious detail concerns Inter’s record in the Brazilian Championship. In six matches without their captain on the pitch, Inter recorded four wins (against Santos, Corinthians, Fluminense and Vasco) and just two defeats (against Cruzeiro and Mirassol). By contrast, in the 27 league matches in which Alan Patrick featured, the team registered four wins, 11 draws and 12 defeats. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Colandrea Passes on the Press Conference after the Offense Passed on Scoring Points – The Morning After
item.description: First things first. If you are the starting quarterback at Nebraska and you just re-signed for another year for allegedly $6 million, then you come out to the press conference and take some arrows for your team. Moving On. We all knew last night was coming and that is the problem with this football program. Nebraska’s defense completely dominated the game, but just like against Indiana, it was two plays the defense surrendered which made all the difference. We should not require the Nebraska defense to play perfectly in order to win football games against teams like Washington. Earlier this week Dana Holgorsen said that it felt like it was a race to 21 points in order to win a Big Ten football game. He made it about one-third of the way. It is almost ironic and comical that after the report about Nebraska re-signing Anthony Colandrea for next year, he then throws two interceptions in his first three passes of the game. It was like we should have expected it. Anthony Colandrea was not the only problem. The entire offense was the problem last night. Whenever there were a few steps forward then we would see several steps back. Whether it was drops or extremely badly timed penalties on big gains (which has happened all year). Or when Nebraska gets away from running the ball with the running backs. This is probably the best defense we have seen since the Pelini years. This offense is ruining a potentially program-changing season in front of them. Nebraska had a great opportunity to be 8-2. They were favored by 7.5 or 8.5. They dominated the game for nearly 3.75 quarters. However, again, the problem is that Nebraska fans knew what was coming. They knew exactly what was going to happen. It felt inevitable. I was saying during the entire second half that the Nebraska defense was going to have to get a turnover or a score for Nebraska to win and it didn’t happen. The Morning After Steven Sipple: Nebraska falls for third straight time, and it again feels nightmarish “Welcome to Your Worst Nightmare.” That’s what the banner in Nebraska’s student section cautioned Saturday night at Memorial Stadium, aimed at the visiting Washington Huskies. This was a nightmare, all right. For the home team. What we learned from Nebraska’s loss to Washington Nebraska had yet another golden opportunity to kickstart the second half of its season. For the third straight game, it suffered another brutal defeat. Here are our five biggest takeaways from the Huskers’ 17-10 loss to Washington and what it means for head coach Matt Rhule and Co. going forward… Rhule postgame comments after Huskers lose it again in the fourth quarter It feels the same, but there’s always some odd road taken to this dark place. This week’s strange, haunting path included a fourth-and-18 conversion by Washington when one stop by the Blackshirts would’ve basically won it. But of course. item.description: Fenerbahce v Besiktas - Turkish Super League - Getty Images Sport Ole Gunnar Solskjaer insists Michael Carrick is still the right man to take Manchester United forward, despite a nine-game winless run that has left them 17th in the Premier League. Solskjaer also revealed he offered to step in after Ruben Amorim's sacking in January, but spoke highly of Carrick, his former assistant, when the club were weighing up their options. Solskjaer backs Carrick despite winless run Carrick's side slipped to a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday, as Morgan Rogers struck shortly after half-time and Cole Palmer converted a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was sent off. United are now without a win in nine games, their longest such run since 1988, and sit 17th in the Premier League. Solskjaer, however, remains firmly in Carrick's corner. Speaking to Norwegian outlet TV2, he said: "Michael has what it takes to take that club forward. I think he's the right man. He understands the club, understands the fans, and knows what's required. You don't see that 'devil' in him. But it's there, and I have it too. We are so incredibly alike." Solskjaer recommended Carrick to United chiefs Carrick, who played alongside Solskjaer at Old Trafford and later worked as his assistant, was named caretaker boss after Amorim's sacking in January. He was then handed the job permanently after guiding United to third place and Champions League qualification, and Solskjaer revealed he had put in a good word for his former team-mate. "Perhaps not many people thought I would become a football coach, certainly not the manager of Manchester United. Many probably thought the same about Michael Carrick," he said. "When I spoke with United, I also spoke highly of Michael. 'If you choose him, you're getting a good man,' I said. I believe he did the same for me. Neither of us was desperate to get the job. But we'd likely step up if they asked." Solskjaer offered to step in after Amorim exit Solskjaer, who spent three years in charge of United before leaving in 2021, was linked with a return after an unsuccessful spell at Besiktas last season. item.title: Braves predicted to trade Ronald Acuna Jr. for Phillies' $330M two-time MVP in monster deal
item.description: Braves predicted to trade Ronald Acuna Jr. for Phillies' $330M two-time MVP in monster deal originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Braves are entering another crucial offseason after it became clear that their starting rotation wasn't deep enough when it came time for the postseason. The starting pitchers were great, but having to rely on a bullpen game every third game shouldn't be the norm in the playoffs. Now, the Braves have several important decisions to make that could shape the future of the organization. One of those decisions was whether to bring Ozzie Albies and Ronald Acuña Jr. back. On Friday, Atlanta announced that both players would return for the 2027 season. “The Braves today exercised options for OF Ronald Acuña Jr. and INF Ozzie Albies for the 2027 season,” the Braves posted. However, that doesn't mean Acuña is entirely off the trade market. His lack of production as a former MVP has disappointed fans and raised questions about whether Atlanta could move him. Bleacher Report's Zachary D. Rymer believes the Braves could trade Acuña for Philadelphia Phillies superstar Bryce Harper in a blockbuster deal. “Anyway, the rationale starts here: Bryce Harper should probably move on from Philadelphia, and Ronald Acuña Jr. should probably do the same from Atlanta. Things for both players in both places have gotten…weird. So, why not swap the two players? The obvious answer is "Because they're NL East rivals, you fool," and that is fair. Even so, the shoe fits on both ends. The Phillies need youth and a right-handed bat, and the Braves need more present upside than Acuña has shown over the last two years,” Rymer wrote. Harper is starting to feel the pressure as he continues to chase a World Series title in Philadelphia. The two-time MVP did mention that the roster could look different in 2027. “I'd imagine this team is going to look a lot different next year," Harper said. This would be one of the wildest trades in MLB history, as division rivals rarely trade superstars with each other. However, it is a move that could potentially benefit both teams. The biggest obstacle is Harper's $330 million contract with the Phillies . Atlanta typically isn't eager to take on massive contracts, but for a blockbuster swap like this, the potential payoff might make it worth considering. item.title: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer says he would have liked to stay in charge at Man United “forever”
item.description: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer says he would have liked to stay in charge at Man United “forever” Former Manchester United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer has revealed juicy details about his interview for the caretaker job earlier this year. The Norwegian and Michael Carrick both applied for the position following Ruben Amorim’s departure. The Englishman was chosen for the job, helped the Red Devils secure third place in the Premier League and ultimately bagged the full-time role. Unfortunately, Carrick has struggled to replicate that form this campaign, with his team now 17th in the league table after nine games, with just one win under the belt. The Englishman was expected to face the sack after Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at the hands of Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, but United continue to back him for now. With several managerial candidates tipped as possible replacements, Solskjaer has opened up on his former team-mate’s situation at the Theatre of Dreams. Solskjaer opens up on interviewing for caretaker position When asked by TV2 if he missed being United manager, Solskjaer responded: “Yes, well, sitting here like this… There were some fantastic moments, but everything in its own time. I do miss it, yes. I’d have liked to have stayed there forever, but life goes on.” The Norwegian went on to shed light on applying for the caretaker position earlier this year, which eventually went to Carrick. He said: “When I spoke to United, I spoke highly of Michael as well. ‘If you choose him, you’ll get a good man,’ I said. I think he did the same with me.” “Neither of us was desperate to get the job. We’d probably step up if they asked. At that particular time, the talk was of being an interim manager for the rest of the season.” Solskjaer insisted that had he taken the job, it would only have been until the summer, adding: “Going back to the way things were isn’t always such a good idea. Yes, I would have taken the job, but I hadn’t intended it to last any longer than until the summer. It was probably time for someone else to have a go.” Solskjaer rubbishes rumours of ‘demands’ Some reports suggested that Carrick was chosen ahead of Solskjaer because the Norwegian made greater demands than the former. However, the ex-United manager refuted those claims, stating: “No, that’s just nonsense!” “I had a nice chat with Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada. We didn’t discuss contract length or anything like that. I was available if needed and didn’t make any demands. I gave my views on what needs to be done for the club to move forward. item.title: Skip Bayless believes Malachi Toney’s presence makes it ‘hard to evaluate’ QB Darian Mensah
item.description: Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Skip Bayless has made a huge admission about the Miami Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah, stating that it was hard for the veteran analyst to evaluate him due to his superstar wide receiver teammate Malachi Toney. Mensah had a top game against Bill Belichick’s North Carolina, recording 274 passing yards and scoring 3 touchdowns. With the game hanging in the balance, Mensah connected with Malachi Toney on a 9-yard TD pass to give Miami a 38-28 lead. Although UNC responded with a touchdown of their own, Miami was able to hold on and grabbed a 38-35 win to maintain their unbeaten record. The QB-WR duo has been impressive for Miami, leading the best offensive unit in College Football. While Toney has received a lot of praise for his performances, Mensah has also been one of the best QBs, throwing at an 81.4% completion rate. Despite his accuracy and impact in Miami’s win against UNC, Toney’s brilliance continues to overshadow Mensah’s performances. Skip Bayless believes Malachi Toney’s brilliance makes it difficult to evaluate Mensah Malachi Toney has recorded 73 receptions for 1,027 yards while also scoring 13 touchdowns. Jeremiah Smith and Toney have been the wide receivers who have grabbed all the headlines. While Toney’s brilliance has helped him break several school records, Mensah has been putting up efficient performances and climbing up the draft rankings. He is expected to be one of the top QBs drafted in the 2027 NFL Draft. However, Bayless is not really ready to buy the hype around the Miami quarterback. “Malachi Toney is so good that it’s hard to evaluate Darian Mensah. I think he’s very good but Toney would make a lot of pretty good QBs look better than they should,” Bayless wrote on X. Mensah has thrown only 1 interception in 8 games, which is sensational for a college quarterback. In the NFL, efficiency is a key metric for a QB and so far Mensah has shown that he is highly reliable and can take care of the ball. The presence of Toney makes it easier for him, but Mensah is still a top quarterback and has proven that he can lead a top offence in CFB. The two teammates are going to be contenders for the Heisman Trophy, but it will be interesting to see who triumphs, as both have put up sensational numbers already. More importantly, it helped Dallas establish an offensive identity that had been missing during its consecutive losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay. item.description: Photo by Christina Pahnke - sampics/Corbis via Getty Images | Corbis via Getty Images Bayern Munich faced Borussia Dortmund and drew 2-2 at the Allianz Arena. The match brought bad news, with Bayern losing two players within the first half hour. Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari were both injured during the game, joining a long list of sidelined players. Later, Michael Olise also exited early, causing further concern. While having a large injury list is not necessarily a new problem for Bayern or club football in general, there is heightened anxiety regarding Bayern’s specific situation. Currently, the Bavarians have five out of their seven starting attackers injured. This is particularly worrying because those seven attackers cover just four positions. With fans calling for new signings in the January transfer window, CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen was asked whether the club might finally add players rather than assuming they are invincible to injuries. Dreesen responded by stating that it was too early for that discussion, citing players like Luis Diaz, Jamal Musiala, and Michael Olise, whose recovery timelines remain uncertain. “Lucho will be out for four to six weeks. He is making good progress and has resumed running training,” the CEO said, per Sky Sport and @iMiaSanMia . “Jamal will return. We also need to see what exactly is going on with Olise; it’s difficult to say at this stage. I think we shouldn’t rush into discussing these kinds of topics.” Naturally, fans are unlikely to take this well. Bayern soon face Atlético Madrid and several other tough opponents in both domestic and European competitions, alongside the ongoing risk of players picking up injuries on international duty. It may not be far-fetched for Bayern to consider reinforcing the full-back, defensive midfield, and wing positions, rather than continually assuming a full squad will be available outside of rare exceptions like this one. item.title: Former Bradford City chairman Richmond, 85, dies
item.description: Geoffrey Richmond oversaw Bradford's promotion to the Premier League in 1999 [Getty Images] The former chairman of Bradford City, Geoffrey Richmond, has died at the age of 85. Richmond helped oversee the Bantams' promotion to the Premier League in 1999, marking the first time the club had played in the top flight for 77 years. Announcing his death on Sunday, the club said Richmond had also "played an important role in the redevelopment" of its Valley Parade ground during his eight years as chairman. A City spokesperson added: "The thoughts of everyone at Bradford City AFC are with Geoffrey's family and friends at this difficult time." Richmond, who was born in Leeds and also served as chairman of Scarborough, took over at Valley Parade in 1994. The club was promoted to the First Division two years later after beating Notts County in a play-off final on its Wembley debut, before reaching the top flight in 1999. A famous David Wetherall header against Liverpool ensured survival on the final day of the season, but the club was relegated the following year after spending big on wages for players such as Benito Carbone and Stan Collymore. With the club in financial turmoil, Richmond left in 2002. Paying tribute on X, football reporter Alan Biggs described Richmond as "a larger than life figure in every sense" and "charismatic and controversial in equal measure". He added: "Can only speak from personal experience; provided many a story. Friendly, though could be cantankerous if you disagreed with him eg. over manager turnover." The Leeds-based New Rover Cricket Club, where Richmond was also a chairman and player, said he had played a "significant role" in its history. The club, based in Adel, said: "His contribution to New Rover, both on and off the field, will never be forgotten. "He was a valued member of our club family, and his commitment helped shape the club we are proud to be today." item.description: Waiting on the tarmac for an airport crew to de-ice their plane, one thing was clear to James Brooks and his San Diego Chargers teammates. “I said, 'I’m never coming back to Cincinnati because this place is too cold,’” Brooks said. “I had never experienced anything like that cold.” The Chargers were eager to get out of Cincinnati following the AFC Championship Game on Jan. 10, 1982, a contest that became known as the Freezer Bowl. The game at Riverfront Stadium was famous for windchills that dropped to around -60 degrees. The Bengals won, too. For the Chargers, a playoff run that started in thrilling fashion came crashing down in the Southwest Ohio cold. A week earlier, San Diego stunned head coach Don Shula’s Miami Dolphins , eliminating them in an overtime thriller at the Orange Bowl. The victory wasn’t the Super Bowl propellant they’d hoped it would be, and Brooks, whose rookie season ended with the loss to the Bengals in an unforgettable cold, simply wanted to go home. Less than three years later, Cincinnati became home for Brooks, but he said he couldn’t believe it when his agent called to tell him he’d be going back to the site of the Freezer Bowl via trade. “When they traded for me, really, I thought it was a joke. I was like, ‘really?’,” Brooks said. “I said, ‘I’m not sure I want to be in Cincinnati.’… (Bengals head coach) Sam Wyche called me and I’m like, I didn’t know who Sam Wyche was. I didn’t have any idea.” During an Oct. 27 interview with The Enquirer, Brooks said coming to Cincinnati was the best thing that ever happened to him. At 5-foot-10 and about 180 pounds during his playing days, Brooks might have been a diminutive figure on NFL fields. His play suggested otherwise, particularly in Cincinnati where from 1984 to 1991 he became one of the best running backs of his era, as well as the Bengals’ all-time leading rusher (6,447 yards). Multiple generations of Bengals fans are familiar with Ickey Woods, a second-round pick in the 1988 NFL Draft. That's thanks in part to the proliferation of Woods' signature touchdown celebration and modern commercials featuring the "Ickey Shuffle." Younger fans might not realize that Woods was drafted to eventually replace Brooks. At least that's how Brooks saw it, and with good reason. During Brooks' age-30 season in 1988, the 22-year-old Woods out-rushed him with 1,066 yards and 16 touchdowns to Brooks' 931 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. Unfortunately, injuries derailed Woods' career, and he was out of the game after the 1991 season. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers offensive lineman Spencer Anderson during a playoff game against the Houston Texans on Jan. 12, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — After a sluggish start from their running game over the first couple weeks of the season, the Pittsburgh Steelers have adjusted and have hit the ground running ever since Jaylen Warren’s dominant performance against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3. And the running attack has continued as the Steelers dominated the New Orleans Saints on the ground in Paris last week, and head coach Mike McCarthy pulled a trick out of his hat when he used a familiar tactic that the 2025 Steelers offense often utilized by reintroducing the “Jumbo” package , using backup guard Spencer Anderson as a sixth offensive lineman. On 13 snaps out of the Jumbo package, they ran the ball 12 times for 77 yards and completed a pass for six yards, which is good enough for 6.4 yards per play. Despite McCarthy’s preference for a heavy passing attack, his decision to borrow from his predecessors and deploy the Jumbo package suggests that he is embracing the ‘bully ball’ football that this current roster excels at. Using heavier formations will make life more difficult for opposing defenses to contend with the one-two punch of Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle , who combined for 222 total yards on 36 touches against the Saints. item.title: Week 9 Report Card: Ducks get back on track vs. Northwestern
item.description: After the most tumultuous week in recent memory for the Oregon Ducks program, they emerged from the adversity and beat the No. 20 Northwestern Wildcats at Autzen Stadium. The Ducks came back from a 20-13 halftime deficit, winning by a final score of 34-26. The Wildcats had the upper hand in the first 30 minutes, with quarterback Aidan Chiles — a Oregon State and Michigan State transfer — dicing them up through the air and evading them with ease with his legs. By halftime, he had amassed over 200 total yards and two touchdowns, one passing and one rushing. He looked unstoppable, but that was until the Oregon defensed tightened the screws once they came back from the break. The Wildcats managed just six points in the second half, while Oregon's offense came alive despite the absences of star running backs Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. to injuries. In their place, true freshman running back Brandon Smith emerged with over 100 total yards and a touchdown, proving vital to the Ducks' offense in a relief outing. Quarterback Dylan Raiola looked sharp for the most part, surpassing 300 yards and three touchdowns through the air. Let's dive into this week's report card, featuring grades and analysis for every position group. But this week, with the coaching staff being the main topic since the Ducks last took the field, we evaluated the coaches first. Coaching Grade: B+ It was a tale of two halves for the coaches on both sides of the ball. In the first half, the offense led by playcaller Jay Johnson couldn't get out of first gear, settling for a pair of field goals in the red zone. The defense, meanwhile, had major trouble corralling Chiles and his top wide receiver, Griffin Wilde, who kept finding open space in the middle areas of the field. But some adjustments were made at halftime, as the Ducks outscored the Wildcats 21-6 in the final 30 minutes, with the offense flowing much more easily as they took shots down the field and the defense, led by Chris Hampton, closed the pocket in on Chiles, negating his creativity and play-making abilities. It was probably a "C-" performance from the coaches in the first half and an "A" in the second half, so a "B+" feels about right. Quarterbacks Grade: B+ There were still some scary moments, namely the fumble on the third play for Raiola, but he rebounded nicely and put together a 22-completion, 336-yard, three-touchdown game after weeks of abysmal play. item.title: Referee accidentally fractures college football player's leg
item.description: The incident happened at East Carolina Pirates' Dowdy–Ficklen Stadium [Getty Images] A referee accidentally fractured a college football player's leg during a bizarre incident in the first half of East Carolina Pirates' win against Temple Owls. East Carolina defensive back David Coleman Jr was standing on the field with team-mates in between plays, when an official ran in to address something near the 40-yard line. As the official approached the players from behind, he slipped and slid into Coleman Jr, who fell forward to the ground. Coleman Jr stayed on the turf, before eventually being helped from the field by two team members, who carried him so he did not have to put weight on his injured leg. East Carolina coach Blake Harrell later confirmed Coleman Jr had an X-ray at half-time which showed he fractured his fibula during the incident. "Our thoughts and our prayers are with him. But that's just one of those things. Kind of wild it happens, I'd never seen that from an official," said Blake. item.title: Spence 'very proud' to break WSL appearance record
item.description: Drew Spence was named Tottenham captain in the summer [Getty Images] Tottenham midfielder Drew Spence says it is a "very proud moment" to become the Women's Super League's all-time appearance record holder. Spence, 34, started in Tottenham's WSL game against Birmingham City on Sunday, making her 217th appearance in the competition. She overtook ex-Chelsea captain Millie Bright and could become the only outfield player at Tottenham to play 90 minutes in all of their WSL games this season. "I've been around for a while! I'm incredibly proud to be able to do that and it's not just a proud moment for me, but also for my family," Spence told BBC Sport. "It's [about] all the hard work that I put in throughout the years. When you're younger, you don't really think about these types of accolades. "It was all about winning trophies. Now it's happened, it's such a massive part of my career and something that I can be proud of to look back on. "I know the sacrifices - looking after yourself and making sure that you're available all the time. I know how hard it is to keep that motivation for so many seasons." Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed 'I'm in the best shape I've ever been' Spence has played her entire career in London, spending 14 years at Chelsea before making the move to Tottenham in 2022. She progressed from Arsenal and Fulham's academies and swapped nationalities from England to Jamaica in 2021. During her time at Chelsea she won five league titles and four FA Cup trophies as part of one of England's most successful squads. "She was a great team-mate, such a sweet soul off the pitch, but when she got on it, she was an absolute warrior," Chelsea midfielder Erin Cuthbert said. "Technically, she's got the brains and the skillset. She looked after me from the very beginning [although] she welcomed me to the club with a two-footed challenge! "She certainly deserves all the plaudits. To have that longevity is something I look up to. Now, she's a leader at Spurs." Spence was named Tottenham captain in the summer and has gone on to become a key figure under manager Martin Ho. In her first season at the club she played 22 games, more than in any campaign at Chelsea, and she has played every minute so far in 2026-27. "I feel like I'm probably in the best shape that I've ever been. I'm recovering quicker, I understand my body a lot more and the nutrition side of things has helped me," said Spence. "It's understanding what is right for me to recover and just little things. We have all those luxuries now which is amazing for the younger players." Drew Spence has overtaken Millie Bright as the WSL appearance record holder [Getty Images] Despite her achievements, Spence admits there are "regrets" from earlier in her career, when she wished she had understood how to prepare her body better. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s just say it right up front – Kirk Ferentz has Luke Fickell and Wisconsin in the torture chamber. And there is no escape in sight. Since Wisconsin’s last win in this series, in 2021 – a football lifetime ago – the Badgers have scored a grand total of two (2) touchdowns and 26 points against Iowa. They scored a touchdown late in the first half of the 2022 game, and early in the fourth quarter of the 2024 game. Two in five meetings. The margin the last five years is 148-26. Since that late 2024 touchdown, Iowa’s on an 81-0 run against the Badgers. “81-0 run” really rolls off the tongue. They managed to go eight (8) quarters without scoring a single point against the Hawks. Eight quarters . Two games! Iowa with consecutive shutouts against the Badgers – what a time to be alive! Wisconsin hasn’t been shut out in consecutive games against an opponent since Michigan from 1977-1980. Neither team’s done this in the series before. It’s crazy just how much Iowa’s in their heads. This feels a bit like the mid-90s, when no matter how good Wisconsin was, they couldn’t beat Iowa. Just couldn’t do it. And that’s part of what makes this so shocking. Wisconsin dipped some as a program, but they feel like they’re improving and back on a solid trajectory under Fickell. They (mostly) look the part again. item.description: Bob Trumpy had a knack for getting his way, whether he was convincing Cincinnati Bengals coaches to run an off-script deep route or spearheading the movement to beat the heat during training camp at Wilmington College. The latter required a little ingenuity. During grueling summer training camps in Wilmington, players weren't allowed to have window air conditioners in their dorm rooms. Trumpy and roommate Bob Johnson, the team's first-ever draft pick , found a workaround that would benefit everyone. Trumpy and Johnson had a friend in Glendale, Melna Burchenal , who owned a window unit that wasn't technically an air conditioner. They brought it to Wilmington, where its power surge caused the lights in the dorm to dim. "Everyone had one," Johnson said. "That was completely from Trumpy's chutzpah." That is arguably one of Trumpy's biggest contributions to the Bengals, but his stellar 10-year career on the field is why the late tight end will be inducted into the Bengals Ring of Honor alongside James Brooks on Sunday, Nov. 1.
